newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bank traces owners of dormant WWII accounts.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bank traces owners of dormant WWII accounts.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) said on Friday it had tracked down rightful owners for around a third of the 10 million Swiss francs ($6.8 million) in dormant World War Two-era accounts it has found in a sweep of its books.
But chief executive Mathis Cabiallavetta held out scant hope of finding more unclaimed wealth that Jewish groups believe Swiss banks may be harbouring from the families of Holocaust victims.

In remarks prepared for delivery at a news conference on UBS's 1996 results. Cabiallavetta said the bank was fully committed to working with a independent panel set up by Swiss bankers and Jewish groups last May to search for dormant wealth.
"It must be said, however, that it is unlikely that any vast amounts, to be distributed to any potential heirs of Holocaust victims, will be uncovered," he said.

UBS, under fire from critics for accidentally shredding old documents amid the probe, has identified in the most recent search 10 million francs in accounts opened before 1945 but whose owners have not been in touch for more than 10 years.

Of the 10 million, "We managed to trace the rightful heirs to assets in dormant accounts amounting to approximately 3.5 million francs thanks to the opening of up of Eastern Europe and the fact that this gave us access to certain documents for the first time," Cabiallavetta said.
"None of those traced were heirs of Holocaust victims, however," he added.
One bank official who asked not to be named said the 3.5 million francs came largely from two accounts held by people who died shortly after the war, but he did not give any more information.
